author: Al Jazeera English
description:
The International Court of Justice (ICJ) in The Hague marks 80 years of attempting to resolve international conflicts through law rather than war.

Correspondent Step Vaessen reports from the Peace Palace on the court's history and its impact on international law. The ICJ has handled more than 200 cases and issued 150 binding judgments, but its authority can be challenged when states reject or fail to implement its rulings.

The report examines landmark cases involving the US intervention in Nicaragua and the Srebrenica genocide, as well as the ongoing South Africa v. Israel case concerning Gaza.

UN Secretary-General António Guterres says international law is being violated “before our eyes”. Expert Iva Vukusic says the court's effectiveness ultimately depends on whether states are willing to act on its rulings.

Al Jazeera's Step Vaessen reports.

description: UN funding shortages and cuts to aid contributions are forcing humanitarian agencies to scale back operations, leaving refugees with less support. Ismail first arrived in Kakuma in 2011 before returning to Sudan to study physiotherapy, but was displaced again by the war that began in 2023. She returned to the camp without completing the process of becoming a licensed physiotherapist and now works with Humanity & Inclusion, supporting people with disabilities. Ismail says around 60 percent of the aid previously available to refugees has been cut, leaving only about 40 percent of UNHCR support. She says most of the small income she receives goes towards food, leaving little for other needs. author: Al Jazeera English
description:
UNRWA has long provided education, healthcare and aid to Palestinians in Gaza, but Israeli restrictions have left much of its network non-functional. Before the war, 300,000 children attended 288 UNRWA-run schools; many now shelter displaced families instead. Of 22 healthcare centres once operating across the Strip, only six remain active, leaving patients with chronic illnesses struggling to access medicine. The agency says it can no longer bring in aid independently, relying instead on international partners for supplies.

Al Jazeera’s Tareq Abu Azzoum reports from Khan Younis, Gaza.
